text:
maria: Heads-up — after upgrading to redwood-inference-js@1.6.0 our Jest + Vitest runs started failing in CI. Local node 18 fine, CI (ubuntu-lts) fails with import errors.
aj: can you paste the error?
maria: ```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at internalCompileFunction (node:internal/vm:... )
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:...)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:...)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:...)
    at Function.Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:...)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:...)
    at require (node:internal/modules/cjs/helpers:...)
    at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/redwood-inference-js/dist/index.mjs:1:1)
```
samir: looks like CI is trying to require an ESM entry (index.mjs) from a CJS runner. Is your Jest configured to treat .mjs as ESM?
lucy: which runner — jest or vitest? they behave differently.
maria: both. We have unit tests under jest (ts-jest) and e2e using vitest. Vitest fails with `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when mocking the sdk: `jest.mock('redwood-inference-js')` style mocks blow up.
aj: common causes: package has conditional exports that point main->dist/index.mjs, no cjs fallback. package.json likely has "exports" with only import field. Can you paste redwood-inference-js package.json snippet?
maria: snippet: ```json
{
  "name": "redwood-inference-js",
  "version": "1.6.0",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```
samir: yep — no CJS entry. That forces ESM consumers to import, but many test runners still use CJS semantics. Two options: SDK ships a CJS build or tests must treat the package as ESM (hard).
lucy: for vitest you can inline deps to force ESM transform: ```js
// vitest.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: { inline: ['redwood-inference-js'] }
  }
})
```
maria: tried that — vitest gets past import, but mocks behave weird. `vi.mock('redwood-inference-js')` returns actual module shape (named exports/async functions) instead of mock functions. Also had to set `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` in tsconfig otherwise import fails.
aj: for jest with ts-jest you can set `extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts', '.mts', '.mjs']` and use `transform: { '^.+\\.(ts|tsx)$': 'ts-jest' }` plus `jest.config.js` `moduleNameMapper` hack. Ugly.
maria: CI workaround that temporarily fixed it: add node resolver to jest and force transform with `esbuild-jest` for the sdk: ```js
// jest.config.js
module.exports = {
  transform: {
    '^.+\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs)$': 'esbuild-jest'
  },
  transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/(?!(redwood-inference-js)/)']
}
```
ci-bot: Pipeline #4521 — tests failed on ubuntu-lts after upgrade (see above).
samir: Another angle — ask SDK to publish a dual-format bundle (cjs in dist/cjs + module in dist/esm) and add `exports` with conditional points: `{ "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs" }`. That would make both test runners happy.
maria: opened GH issue in redwood-inference-js repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference-js/issues/234 — requesting CJS consumers and test-runner guidance.
lucy: until SDK ships CJS, other workable hacks: 1) use `moduleNameMapper` to point 'redwood-inference-js' -> '<rootDir>/__mocks__/redwood-inference-js.cjs' 2) mock by path to compiled cjs fixture 3) run tests under node12+ ESM-mode (pain).
aj: also check package's `types` — if d.ts references `export =` that can confuse ts-jest. Might need `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports`.
maria: sample minimal repro I pushed to our repo under tools/test-repro: `package.json` sets "type":"commonjs" for the app and installs redwood-inference-js@1.6.0. Repro script: `node -r ts-node/register tests/foo.test.ts` -> fails.
dev-bot: created ticket DEVEX-987 to track recommended test configs and SDK asks.
maria: TL;DR: please prioritize SDK providing a CJS build + a clear "testing" note in README. Meanwhile I'll try inline deps for vitest + esbuild-jest for jest. cc @devx-team :eyes:
aj: +1. Also add a simple guide to our internal devx wiki with concrete jest/vitest snippets and CI tweaks.
samir: i'll add a short RFC asking SDK team to publish dual bundles and include a sample `exports` entry.
maria: thanks — will update thread when CI green. :sparkles:
